blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Philippine stocks slipped further on Monday as escalating tensions in the Middle East, high oil prices and rising local treasury yields kept investors on the sidelines. The benchmark Philippine Stock Exchange Index (PSEi) shed 0.21 percent, or 12.12 points, to close at 5,843.79. READ: US warns of rapid escalation in Middle East war Japhet Tantiangco, research manager at Philstocks Financial Inc., said the market extended its decline as fresh developments in the Middle East weighed on sentiment.
